bib.title: Faithful Logical Reasoning via Symbolic Chain-of-Thought

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Faithful Logical Reasoning via Symbolic Chain-of-Thought" (SymbCoT), Jundong Xu, Hao Fei, Liangming Pan, Qian Liu, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu. The extraction shows only "arXiv:2405.18357v2 [cs.CL] 11 Jun 2024", with no venue printed. I would cite it as an arXiv preprint (2024). The Limitations and Ethics sections look like an ACL submission, but the text does not say so.

COVERAGE: I read all 129,680 chars. The main text (0–~37k) and the appendix text were read in full. The reference list (~37k–48.8k) was skimmed for origins. The appendix prompts (I.1 onward, ~64.6k to the end) were read only at the start, for ProntoQA, and at the end. The middle is repeated per-dataset few-shot prompts. The extraction is clean, but figure data (Figs 3–10) is only partly numeric.

CLAIMS
- Claim: SymbCoT is a four-module prompting pipeline (Translator, Planner, Solver, Verifier), all run by the same LLM with few-shot demos per module and no external solver. It translates the premises into first-order logic, plans, solves with named inference rules, then verifies.
  - number: none
  - setup: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613) and GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613). Footnote: "We use few-shot demonstrations for each module."
  - quote: "SymbCoT is entirely facilitated by LLMs without relying on any external reasoners/tools, i.e., encompassing both the initial translation and subsequent reasoning phases."
  - where: p.2, offset ~4k–6k
- Claim: With GPT-4, SymbCoT averages 88.47 on the three first-order-logic datasets. Vanilla CoT averages 79.16 and Logic-LM (LLM translator plus external Prover9 solver) 80.59.
  - number: 88.47 vs 79.16 vs 80.59 (+7.88 over Logic-LM, +9.31 over CoT)
  - setup: GPT-4, accuracy on PrOntoQA (500 items), ProofWriter (600), FOLIO (204). Baselines for Logic-LM and the others are copied from earlier papers using the same records.
  - quote: "SymbCoT 99.60 82.50 83.33 88.47 (+0.81) (+2.84) (+4.41) (+7.88)"
  - where: Table 1, p.5
- Claim: Per dataset with GPT-4, CoT is already near ceiling on PrOntoQA, so the symbolic gain there is small. The gain is larger on FOLIO and ProofWriter.
  - number: PrOntoQA CoT 98.79 vs SymbCoT 99.60; ProofWriter CoT 68.11 vs 82.50; FOLIO CoT 70.58 vs 83.33
  - setup: GPT-4, Table 1
  - quote: "CoT 98.79 68.11 70.58 79.16"
  - where: Table 1
- Claim: With GPT-3.5, SymbCoT beats CoT on average but loses on FOLIO, even to plain CoT. The authors blame non-linear reasoning.
  - number: average 64.22 vs CoT 58.11; FOLIO 57.84 vs CoT 57.35 vs Logic-LM 62.74 (−4.90 vs Logic-LM)
  - setup: GPT-3.5-turbo
  - quote: "SymbCoT 75.80 59.03 57.84 64.22 (+8.00) (+0.70) (-4.90) (+3.53)"
  - where: Table 1, and the text "We notice the only exception is on the FOLIO dataset with GPT-3.5, failing to surpass Logic-LM."
- Claim: The method also works with a constraint-optimization representation. Gains are smaller on AR-LSAT.
  - number: LogicalDeduction 93.00 vs CoT 75.25; AR-LSAT 43.91 vs CoT 35.06; average 68.46 vs CoT 55.14 vs Logic-LM 65.34
  - setup: GPT-4, LogicalDeduction (300 items) and AR-LSAT (230 items)
  - quote: "SymbCoT 93.00 43.91 68.46 (+5.37) (+0.87) (+3.12)"
  - where: Table 2
- Claim: The planning and solving stage contributes most, followed by the translator. The verifier adds a further gain.
  - number: planner+solver +10.4% average, translator +6.3%
  - setup: GPT-4 ablation across all 5 datasets. The Solver cannot be ablated without the Planner. The figure gives averages of about 79.94 / 77.45 / 67.05 / 60.80, which I read as full / without Verifier / without Planner+Solver+Verifier / without all four modules. The extraction does not label the bars, so that mapping is my inference.
  - quote: "the Planner and Solver components are identified as the most influential, enhancing performance by an average of 10.4%, followed by the Translator module, which facilitates a secondary improvement of 6.3%."
  - where: Sec 4.3 and Fig 3
- Claim: The gain over CoT grows with reasoning depth.
  - number: the figure labels 13.7%, 18.1%, 19.7%, 20.6% and 22.3% appear in the extraction, but I cannot tell which depth each belongs to. Do not cite them.
  - setup: GPT-4, ProofWriter, by proof depth, up to depth 5
  - quote: "as the depth increases, the improvement over CoT becomes more pronounced, suggesting that our advantage lies in tackling more challenging issues."
  - where: Sec 5.1, Fig 4
- Claim: The fully LLM-based pipeline never fails to execute. Logic-LM loses cases to symbolic syntax errors, especially on AR-LSAT.
  - number: 100% execution rate; +17.7 points over Logic-LM on average; +67.4% on AR-LSAT
  - setup: execution rate is the share of questions whose symbolic form the solver can run
  - quote: "Notably, our method achieves a remarkable execution success rate of up to 100%. This represents a significant improvement over Logic-LM by an average of 17.7% percentage points."
  - where: Sec 5.2, Fig 5
- Claim: External solvers lose information when translating to logic and so over-predict "Unknown". SymbCoT recovers most of those cases.
  - number: 55.6% of wrongful "unknown" cases on FOLIO were translation faults (information loss 40.7%, information error 14.8%). SymbCoT reduces these errors by 73.3%.
  - setup: FOLIO, Prover9 as the external solver. Logic-LM's CoT fallback was switched off for this analysis (App. E).
  - quote: "We identify that 55.6% of these errors were due to information loss (IL, 40.7%)—where essential details are missed—and information error (IE, 14.8%)—where translations are incorrect. Implementing our methodology reduces these errors by 73.3%"
  - where: Sec 5.3, Fig 6
- Claim: CoT sometimes gets a correct answer from invalid reasoning. A verifier step removed such cases in the authors' audit.
  - number: CoT 6% unfaithful, SymbCoT without Verifier 2%, SymbCoT with Verifier 0%
  - setup: FOLIO, GPT-4 (the faithfulness section does not state the model). Manual check by five CS graduate students with majority vote. The sample size is not stated.
  - quote: "within the CoT, 6% of correct answers resulted from flawed reasoning... In SymbCoT without a Verifier, the rate of such unfaithful reasoning dropped to 2%. Integrating a Verifier, we eliminated unfaithful reasoning entirely"
  - where: Sec 5.4, Fig 7
- Claim: The method gains more from a stronger model than the external-solver approach does.
  - number: +24.3% for SymbCoT going from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4. Other bars in Fig 8 read +23.7, +21.1 and +19.9, but the extraction does not say which method each belongs to.
  - setup: three first-order-logic datasets
  - quote: "shows the most performance boost (24.3%) with our method upon upgrading models."
  - where: Sec 5.5, Fig 8
- Claim: Cost. The method needs a long chain of generated tokens across four calls.
  - number: per-module average output tokens. On AR-LSAT: Translator 323, Planner 627, Solver 654, Verifier 726. On FOLIO: 145 / 313 / 330 / 334.
  - setup: Table 4. Totals are my arithmetic: about 2,330 tokens per item on AR-LSAT and 1,122 on FOLIO.
  - quote: "Translator 324 290 145 176 323 / Planner 198 202 313 251 627 / Solver 214 216 330 282 654 / Verifier 384 353 334 472 726"
  - where: App. G, Table 4
- Claim: Precision, recall and F1 on FOLIO (App. F).
  - number: F1 of 85 vs Logic-LM 82 vs CoT 79. Logic-LM has the highest precision (95 vs SymbCoT 89 vs CoT 81) but the lowest recall (72 vs SymbCoT 81 vs CoT 75).
  - setup: FOLIO, GPT-4 assumed
  - quote: "Logic-LM achieves the highest precision at 95... Logic-LM has a recall rate of 72, which is the lowest among the three models."
  - where: App. F

LIMITS
- Authors concede only two limits. They tested only two symbolic forms (first-order logic and constraint optimization). The method is costly: "an extended reasoning chain and, consequently, the generation of an increased number of tokens".
- Sec 5.6 says the method fixes invalid inference steps but not path-finding: "our approach does not enhance the model's planning capabilities... the LLM needs to meet this reasoning baseline for SymbCoT to be effective." Appendix A adds that the main failure is picking the wrong reasoning path, and proposes a hybrid with an external solver as future work, untested.
- It loses to Logic-LM on FOLIO with GPT-3.5.
- Baselines (Logic-LM, CoT-SC, ToT, CR, DetermLR) are copied from earlier papers, not re-run. CoT-SC, ToT, CR and DetermLR have no numbers on PrOntoQA or AR-LSAT.
- Only GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (0613 snapshots) were tested. No reasoning models and no open-weight models. Results are from 2023-era models.
- No cost-matched baseline. CoT-SC is shown for GPT-4 only on ProofWriter, FOLIO and LogicalDeduction, and no results are given at equal token spend.
- The faithfulness audit is small, manual and on FOLIO only. Ablation and depth results are shown in figures, mostly without exact numbers in the text.
- The abstract's "refreshing the current state-of-the-art" claim rests on the copied baselines above.
- Tasks are closed-world logic benchmarks with a true/false/unknown answer. The paper does not show transfer to general prompting.

BUILDS ON
- Wei et al. 2022 (chain-of-thought).
- Pan et al. 2023 (Logic-LM) and Olausson et al. 2023 (LINC), which are LLM-translate-then-external-solver systems. SymbCoT replaces the solver with the LLM.
- Wang et al. 2023a (Plan-and-solve) for the plan-then-solve structure.
- Related structured-CoT work: Hu et al. 2023 (code prompting), Imani et al. 2023 (MathPrompter), Li et al. 2023 (structured CoT for code).
- Baselines: Wang et al. 2023b (self-consistency), Yao et al. 2023 (Tree of Thoughts), Zhang et al. 2023a (Cumulative Reasoning), Sun et al. 2023 (DetermLR).
- Datasets: Saparov and He 2023 (PrOntoQA), Tafjord et al. 2021 (ProofWriter), Han et al. 2022 (FOLIO), Srivastava et al. 2022 (LogicalDeduction), Zhong et al. 2022 (AR-LSAT).

CODE: There is no code in the paper. The repo is https://github.com/Aiden0526/SymbCoT. The prompt templates in the appendix (I.1.1, ProntoQA) are worth keeping:
- Verifier prompt, p.4: "Please verify: 1) the symbolic context is consistent with the natural language; 2) the solving step is logically valid."
- Planner prompt, App. I.1.1: "Can you derive a step-by-step plan that can use the premises and First-Order Logic inference rules to infer new knowledge if needed, in order to prove the statement? Start with identifying the goal and break down the necessary logical inference step by step."
- Solver prompt, App. I.1.1: "execute each step by selecting relevant premises and making inference based on First-Order Logic inference rules to solve the question. Ensure to follow the plan and indicate what First-Order Logic inference rules you used."
- Hybrid format: natural-language premises are paired with their symbolic form, for example "If a cartoon character is yellow, it is from the Simpsons ::: ∀x (Yellow(x) → Simpsons(x))".

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): CoT versus SymbCoT on one FOLIO item. CoT reasons "Descampe is from Belgium, so he is in the six-way tie" (overgeneralization), while SymbCoT answers Unknown using existential instantiation. It is the fastest illustration of why symbolic steps expose fallacies.
- Fig 2 (p.2): the pipeline of Translator, Planner, Solver and Verifier.
- Fig 3: ablation bars by dataset.
- Fig 4: gain over CoT by proof depth.
- Fig 5: execution rate against Logic-LM.
- Fig 6: error breakdown of an external solver.
- Fig 7: faithful, unfaithful and false answer shares.
- Fig 8: gain from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4.
- Fig 9: share of predicted True/False/Unknown on FOLIO.
- Fig 10: precision, recall and F1.
- I did not run the caption extractor. These captions come from the text extraction.

PROBLEMS
- No instructions embedded in the PDF.
- Figure numbers (Figs 3, 4, 5, 6, 8) are scrambled in the extraction. The legend-to-value mapping is inferred where noted, and the depth labels in Fig 4 are unassigned.
- Venue is not printed. I did not fill it from memory.
- Sec 4.2 quotes "gains of 21.56%, 6.11%, 3.53% on GPT-3.5, and 22.08%, 9.31% and 7.88% on GPT-4" without saying whether they are absolute points or relative. Average-column differences suggest they are absolute points.
- Table 1 SymbCoT averages of 64.22 and 88.47 are consistent with the per-dataset values.
- Fig 5 and Fig 8 give no per-dataset values in the text.
- Relevance to `/Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/01-prompt-engineering/notes/03-core-techniques.md`: the note's CoT section cites Sprague et al., who find that logic and symbolic tasks benefit from CoT. This paper is evidence on that "logic" side. It is also a plan-then-solve variant to set beside the note's Plan-and-solve paragraph (the note line 147 cites no Wang et al. paper).
